summary.en: Syrian security forces are expanding anti-ISIS raids and targeting former regime loyalists while private security firms support a new Syrian security mogul, and they are disrupting drug-smuggling attempts on the Iraq and Jordan borders. Israeli drones struck a Syrian operative planning attacks for Iran near the Lebanon border, prompting a UN Security Council call for respect of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement. The Syrian army began destroying chemical weapons stockpiles and the UK allocated $90 million to support Syria's economic recovery. Jordan and Syria’s foreign ministers discussed bilateral ties and regional developments. 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Syriske sikkerhetsstyrker utvider anti-IS-raider og retter seg mot tidligere regimelojalister, mens private sikkerhetsfirmaer støtter en ny syrisk sikkerhetsmogul, og de forstyrrer narkotikasmuglingsforsøk ved Irak‑ og Jordan-grensen. Israelske droner rammet en syrisk operativ som planla angrep for Iran nær Libanon-grensen, noe som førte til at FNs sikkerhetsråd oppfordret til respekt for avtalen fra 1974 om tilbaketrekning. Den syriske hæren begynte å ødelegge lagre med kjemiske våpen, og Storbritannia avsatte 90 millioner dollar til støtte for Syriens økonomiske gjenoppbygging. Jordans og Syriens utenriksministerer diskuterte bilaterale bånd og regionale utviklinger. 2 732 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
